mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the discount rate applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thus depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day moving average during the identified rising rate window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting equity market optimism and higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive relative to the prior 10-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer demand proxies such as the HOUST index (units sold) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from inventory clearing to new orders, supporting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 15% while INDPRO decreases by > 2% over the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns underperform the 200-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 for three consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness, lowering investor confidence and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative across 5 such contraction regimes (average p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, market expectations for future rate cuts are reduced, leading to lower risk premia and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5 percentage points in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during periods of sub-2% inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market, which can fuel equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% while PAYEMS remains flat or increases modestly
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive relative to the prior 10-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both consumer demand (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a dual softening in economic activity, which can trigger a risk-off spiral and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative deviation from the 200-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply-side gauge RSAFS (demand in millions of dollars) falls for three consecutive months, it reflects reduced consumer and business spending, which can depress corporate earnings expectations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative across 5 such demand contractions (average p-value > 0.1).
